notes:
A teacher's own introduction is no longer mistaken for the language of the page.

Docket checks whether a page is written in the language its HTML declares. A page
that says lang="en" and is actually in German is a real defect: screen readers
switch pronunciation on that attribute, and search engines use it to decide who
a page is for.

But a page can carry somebody else's words without being written in their
language. On a tutor marketplace, a profile page is in English and is about a
German teacher, and the teacher's self-introduction is quoted on it in German.
Docket measures the main content of a page, deliberately ignoring navigation and
footers — and on a profile page that leaves the quoted introduction as almost
the whole sample. Seventeen working English pages were reported as being in the
wrong language, and the suggested fix was to relabel them as German, which would
have sent them to the wrong readers.

Docket now reads the page title before contradicting the declaration. A page that
really is a translation translates its title too; a profile page does not,
because the title is the publisher's own words. Where the title is plainly in the
language the page declares, the foreign text is treated as content the page
carries rather than the language it is written in.

A translated page that kept its original title is still reported, because a title
that contradicts the body is the same defect seen from the other side.
